newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds steady at higher levels in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds steady at higher levels in late trade.

text.p: German Bund futures were expected to trade in narrow ranges on Friday after having spent much of Thursday drifting in narrow ranges.
Traders said the market's tone has clearly shifted from the bullishness that marked trade in November and earlier this month and there was some fear of a pull-back.
The DTB March Bund future was up 11 basis points late in the day to 100.08. The 10-year benchmark Bund climbed to 102.65 from 102.36, yielding 5.86 percent.
A slew of U.S. data including CPI, retail sales and jobless claims left little impact on the market.

Traders said they were increasingly unwilling to take long positions with the end of the year approaching and given the market's recent wild swings. "Customers have already pulled out of this volatile market," one trader said.
They said the market was on edge today and will remain so on Friday with EU finance ministers meeting in Dublin to hash out details of the EMU stability pact.

Although traders hold mixed views on the meeting's meaning for Bunds, many believe approval of such a pact would be taken as a sign EMU was moving forward according to plan, lifting prices of bonds from high-yielding countries.
Others, however, believe that approval of a pact and the progress towards EMU that it would mean, should be bad for Bunds. EMU, the reasoning goes, could lead to higher German inflation.

At the least, therefore, most expect Bunds to underperform other European markets, especially the high-yielders, if the stability pact is agreed upon -- no matter what conditions Germany is able to have attached to it.
Otherwise, Bunds are expected to follow Treasuries. The U.S. market has pulled the Bund contract off record highs set a couple weeks ago and threatens to continue to weigh.
The Bund/T-note spread was little changed on the day at 55 basis points compared with 56 basis points at the previous close.

The next major domestic event promises to be the Bundesbank's regular year-end press conference next Thursday. The central bank has historically announced its M3 money supply target corridor for the following year at the event.
